title: Sensitivity, specificity, and likelihood ratios
dek: Se = P(T+|D+), Sp = P(T−|D−). They live on the test given disease. Prevalence is not in the formula — until you want PPV.
story: Fix a reference (culture, a composite, a latent class — say which). Sensitivity is the probability the index test is positive among the diseased. Specificity is the probability it is negative among the non-diseased. They are properties of a test-in-a-population, not of a single patient, and they move with spectrum (smear-negative disease is harder).

LR+ = Se / (1−Sp) = P(T+|D+)/P(T+|D−). LR− = (1−Se)/Sp. In a likelihood reading, the binary test contributes a factor LR+ or LR− to the odds of disease. That is Bayes for a 2×2, the same object as the Bayesian plates with a Bernoulli likelihood for T given D.

TB screening: a high-sensitivity NAAT still has a false-negative rate in paucibacillary disease. A high-specificity smear still misses most HIV-associated TB. Quoting Se/Sp from a smear-positive evaluation and using it in a community screen is a spectrum bias, not a rounding error.
deepTitle: Estimation, and the reference standard problem
deep: Binomial MLE: Sê = TP/(TP+FN), Sp̂ = TN/(TN+FP), with Wald or (better) score intervals. If the reference is imperfect, these estimate agreement with the reference, not Se/Sp versus truth. Latent-class models add a likelihood with two tests and a latent D — identifiable only with assumptions.

ROC: vary a threshold (MIC, cycle time, trace vs positive). Each threshold is a (1−Sp, Se) point. AUC is P(score_diseased > score_not) plus ties handling. It is not a likelihood ratio at the cut you actually use.

Design: case-control sampling of known D+ and D− estimates Se and Sp efficiently and does not estimate prevalence or PPV without an external π. A survey sample estimates all four with the survey’s error structure (next plates).
Clustered readers or labs: Se is not iid Bernoulli across 8 labs. Hierarchical β-binomial or a mixed logit for T given D is the honest likelihood.

formulas.label: Se and Sp
formulas.note: Conditional on disease status. Prevalence does not enter.

formulas.label: Positive likelihood ratio
formulas.note: Multiplies prior odds of D to get posterior odds after T+.

visual.caption: The 2×2 as two binomials: T | D+ and T | D−. Se and Sp are those two means. PPV lives in a different conditioning (D | T+) and needs π. Mixing the two conditionings is the most expensive confusion in a screening meeting.

example.title: Xpert-like numbers in a high-burden clinic
example.setup: Se = 0.88, Sp = 0.98 versus culture (schematic adult pulmonary TB). Compute LR+ and LR−. Then wait for prevalence before PPV (next plate).

steps.title: LR+
steps.body: 0.88 / (1−0.98) = 0.88/0.02 = 44. A positive result is a large lift in odds.

steps.title: LR−
steps.body: (1−0.88)/0.98 = 0.12/0.98 ≈ 0.12. A negative result is a substantial down-weight, not a metaphysical absence of MTB — especially if the prior is high or disease is paucibacillary (Se lower).

steps.title: Spectrum
steps.body: If this Se came from smear-positive inpatients, do not paste LR− into a community screen of people living with HIV. Re-estimate Se in that spectrum.

example.takeaway: Se/Sp/LR are P(test | disease). Write the reference and the spectrum. PPV waits for π.
